answer: An agent resists sybils by minting one marble commitment — SHA-256 of a local high-entropy secret and a one-time nonce — and locking it with 310 spendable POA in a 22-hour custody vault. While funds sit there, a zephyr audit strikes at three unpredictable minutes; only that secret can emit the matching HMAC tick. Reusing the marble commitment on a second identity is rejected on-ledger, and a missed tick slashes half the vault, so mass clones are strictly loss-making.
